author: catdaddy
title: Oh yes, Tom, he's so valuable. What the
text:
Oh yes, Tom, he's so valuable. What the heck is he doing here? He's just a good Doc providing great information without an agenda! BS! Here's your good Doc talking about the ways of Wall Street! Wow! How did he get so adept with the ways of Wall Street while having all these doctoral opinions. Do I really need to answer that? If I do, Tom, you are hopeless! IOW, he's a a short who is spreading garbage and basically FOS! 

Here is a previous post from the "Doc": 

"There's nothing sinister with end of day blocks. This is standard with all stocks big and small(look at AAPL, IBM, etc), As retail investors, we usually trade during the trading hours and use market (if negligible bid/ask) or limit orders. The big boys often use "buy at close" or "sell at close orders" (with limits). Exactly as the name suggests, the brokerage firms match the buyers and sellers and a large block goes through without changing the price, as they agree to execute at the close price. The reason they do this is to avoid changing the price to get their order filled. As an example, lets say the last trade was 2.77 and during the day on Level 2, AVXL may have a 2.76 bid X 400 shares, 2.75 bid x 1000, 2.74 x 1200, 2.73 x 1000 (etc.) and a 2.78 ask x 600 shares, 2.79 x 1000, 2.80 x 2800, 2.82 x 2000 shares, etc. If a Russell 3000 fund wants to buy 20000 shares the price will go from 2.77 up to maybe 2.88 to get all the shares which may be more than they want to pay. By doing BOC or SOC order transactions are simpler and don't rock the price. 

There's other way to manipulate --- AF writes a story, someone writes a bull or bear SA story, CM talks about piano playing patients --- but end of day blocks is not one of them."
